Subject: Orcha rd reliability evaluation: failover qualification + demo agenda

Thanks for the convo today, Sam — good alignment on the business drivers and the risk tolerance for failover windows. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can get you a reproducible comparison against the hyperscaler endpoints you mentioned.

Key takeaways from call:
- Orchard must keep <500ms 99th p99 for synchronous inference in regulatory flows; acceptable degradation during region failover is up to 3s for non-critical paths only.
- Primary concerns: transparent error budgets, deterministic rate limit behavior under burst, and controlled failover (drain+redirect) when a region is unhealthy.
- You’ll evaluate both Redwood Dedicated and our hosted API vs the hyperscaler-managed endpoints (their multi-region failover and their autoscaling time to scale).

Redwood proposed test matrix (high level):
1) Baseline latency + p95/p99 at steady state (10k qps/day window) — same model pinned on each provider.
2) Burst test: 3x traffic for 2 minutes — measure tail latency and dropped requests.
3) Region failover (planned): simulate graceful drain of the primary region and measure failover ramp and error budget consumption.
4) Rate limit shaping: apply token-bucket limits and probe behavior for queued vs rejected requests.
5) Cold-start/scale-up: spike from 0 to 500 concurrent streams and measure time-to-stable p95.

Owners/timeline (draft):
- Test plan + scripts: Karthik (deliver by 2026-11-05). Attachment: orchard_failover_test_plan_v1.pdf.
- Run hosted vs hyperscaler: Monica (start 2026-11-09, run for 48h).
- Dedicated config & bench: Ben (provisioned by 2026-11-10, run 11/11–11/12).
- Demo: 30–40m walkthrough with Orch techs to review results, proposed week of 11/16.

Questions for you, Sam:
- Can you share the hyperscaler endpoint details (region, model variant, and any autoscaling knobs)?
- Any restrictions on test accounts or IP allowlists for the Dedicated run?

Next immediate ask from us: sign-off on the test plan and confirm 11/16 demo window availability. I attached the initial test plan and a CSV with demo scenarios.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt

Appreciate the detailed plan, Hannah. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Hyperscaler details: primary region us-east1, failover to us-west1; model is a customer-fine-tuned open-llama-v2 variant we host through their managed endpoint. Their autoscaler is aggressive but they've told us scaling to additional machines can take up to ~2 minutes for large batches.
- For the Dedicated run we will need the IP ranges ahead of time for an allowlist and a short SOC review; Maria will forward the contact for procurement.
- Our main priority is demonstrating predictable tail behavior during cross-region failover for synchronous transactional flows. If Redwood can show both a lower p99 during planned failover and clearer accounting of error budget consumption, that will be the deciding factor.

I can confirm Maria and I are available for a 30–40m demo the week of 11/16 — prefer 11/17 afternoon. Please include a short agenda and test highlights in the invite so we can loop in our SREs.

Thanks — adding technical detail and the concrete scripts we plan to run. I attached the test plan PDF with per-check command lines and metrics to capture. High-level notes: 

Planned verification steps and pass/fail criteria:
- Baseline (steady state): run 60m at nominal qps. Pass if p99 hosted <= 500ms and no request error rates >0.05%.
- Burst (3x for 2m): measure percentage of requests queued vs 429s; pass if dropped requests <0.5% and p99 < 1s after burst.
- Region failover (planned drain): graceful drain + redirect to secondary. We will cause the primary region to report unhealthy endpoints and observe 1) time until client-visible failover complete, 2) error budget consumed per-minute. Pass if mean failover time <3s for synchronous flows and error budget burn is within your stated tolerance.
- Rate-limit shaping: we will test three token-bucket settings (10k/s, 50k/s, 100k/s) and look for consistent rejection semantics (429 + Retry-After header).
- Telemetry: we'll push request tracing headers so we can slice by user/route and produce per-route SLO reports.

Test infra and scripts (owners):
- loadgen harness, k6 + custom client: Karthik
- telemetry ingestion + dashboards: Monica
- Dedicated provisioning and config tuning: Ben

Schedule note: to reduce noise, start Hosted vs Hyperscaler runs in parallel on 11/09 and schedule Dedicated run after the hosted baseline completes. Monica/Ben please confirm resource availability.

Attachment: orchard_failover_test_plan_v1.pdf
